$Comment: The Scarak Brood Queen's fight, run by the game's own encounter scripts, at a site a server owner
chooses once. The pack ships the arena as the MMOSkillQuestPack/Sands_Brood_Queen_Spawners prefab
(the queen's clutch and five brood clutches, each a block that keeps a spawn marker alive) and
this script; the owner pastes the prefab where the fight belongs and stands this script up on it
with /zigencounter spawn Sands_Brood_Queen_Encounter, once per world. The encounter entity is
saved with the world and wakes on its own from then on. The script raises the queen, runs her
three phases and her brood, and tells the Ziggfreed Common library every beat through the zc:
signals, which is how the party's health scale and credit work, how the loot is paid, and how the
notices in Server/ZiggfreedCommon/FeedbackMoments/Sands_Brood_Queen_*.json fire. What the server
owes for the fight (the party scale, the loot, the leaderboard, the map marker, the notices) is
the binding row Server/ZiggfreedCommon/Encounters/Sands_Brood_Queen_Encounter.json; nothing about
the fight itself is written anywhere but here and in the three Sands_Brood_Queen roles.
The shape follows Ziggfreed Common's Zc_Encounter_Base and adds the phase states the base leaves
to a script of its own. The first two instructions run every tick beside whatever state the
fight is in: the Player sensor keeps the roster the boss bar, the scale and the credit read
(eighty blocks around the site, so a bow at the edge of the arena still counts), and
TriggerSpawners raises the queen from the Sands_Brood_Queen_Marker while the fight is in Intro
and no boss is bound yet. Nothing here runs while nobody is near: the site's chunk sleeps with
the rest of the world, and the script picks up where it was when a player walks back in. The
release, on the Target sensor alone, makes the queen vulnerable, puts the bar up under her name,
sends zc:engaged and moves into Phase_1; it keys on the bound boss and never on a beacon.
Intro also carries the fight's safety net: if no queen has bound within the Timeout below (her
marker still resting after the last kill, a missing clutch, a role that failed to load), the
script sends zc:mmoquestpack:no_show and retires to Complete, and a listener can notice a boss
that never rose. The countdown stops the instant a boss binds. A player who waits at a resting
site sees this loop: no_show, Complete's wait, another try.
The phases. Phase_1 is the queen as spawned. At half her health the role changes in place to
Sands_Brood_Queen_Phase2 (the engine keeps her aggro, her target slot and her current health
across the change; only the maximum re-rolls), zc:phase:Phase_2 goes out, and the first brood
of three rises from the Sands_Brood_Marker clutches. At half of what she carried into Phase_2
she changes to Sands_Brood_Queen_Phase3, with a brood of four. Each phase role's MaxHealth is
authored as the health she carries into that phase, so the bar reads full at every phase start
and the three phases together add up to the first role's 1200: the party deals 600 in Phase_1,
300 in Phase_2 and 300 in Phase_3, before the binding row's party scale. Retune the first role to
lengthen the whole fight, retune HealthRange here to move where the phases begin. Count on the
broods is how many clutches fire; a clutch whose spawn is still alive does not fire again, so
five stamped clutches cap the live brood at five however the waves fall. She also calls two
fighters of her own the moment she is alerted and hatches lice through the fight, which is the
template's doing and not this script's.
The defeat beat sits in every phase, because the queen can fall in any of them: when the Target
sensor loses the boss the bar comes down, the slot is released, zc:defeated goes out and the
script retires to Complete. The library settles the credit the instant the death lands, so the
beat here is the authoritative place the bar comes down. Every Target sensor reaches 256 blocks
from the encounter entity, far past anywhere the queen will follow a party (she holds her ground
and throws), because a boss beyond the range would read as a defeat and pay out.
A party that dies or walks off leaves her standing, and that is the other half of an open-world
fight. The library settles the run as a wipe once nobody has been in the roster for the binding
row's WipeGraceSeconds; a little after that, each phase's last instruction (no player within
eighty blocks for the Timeout there) takes the bar down and moves to Standing, where the queen
waits, wounded, with her slot still bound. The next player to come within eighty blocks sends
zc:reset, which opens a fresh run, and Intro's release puts the bar back up and re-engages her
at the health she was left with. Keep that Timeout at or above WipeGraceSeconds so the library
has settled the wipe before the script stands down. Should the queen be gone while Standing, the
defeat beat there retires the script to Complete the same way a kill does.
Complete is the site's rest: the Timeout there is how long after the fight ends the script
waits before it sends zc:reset and returns to Intro to try the marker again. It is one of two
gates on the next fight, and the smaller one; the queen's own marker keeps its own cadence (one
in-game day after she dies, SpawnAfterGameTime in Sands_Brood_Queen_Marker), and both must pass
before she rises again. Turn the marker to change how often she comes back; turn this Timeout
only to change how long the site rests right after a kill. There is no fight music here; the
pack ships no music of its own.
Override this file by id from your own pack to change the fight for every server, or retune the
queen's roles under Server/NPC/Roles/MMOSkillQuestPack for the numbers alone. Keep the file name
distinct from every NPC role's: an encounter script and a role share one id namespace, and a
script named after a role replaces that role at load.
